chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from al-Fudayl, who said:

I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: “Whoever confesses against himself before the Imam regarding a hadd from among the hudud of Allah, one single time, whether he is free or a slave, or whether she is a free woman or a bondwoman, then it is upon the Imam to carry out the hadd upon him for that which he confessed against himself, whoever he may be, except the muhsan fornicator, for he is not stoned until four witnesses testify against him. Then when they testify, he administers to him the hadd of one hundred lashes and then stones him.”

He said, and Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: “And whoever confesses against himself before the Imam regarding a hadd from among the hudud of Allah in matters involving the rights of the Muslims, then it is not upon the Imam to carry out upon him the hadd that he confessed to in his presence until the holder of the right, or his guardian, comes and demands his right.”

He said: Then some of our companions said to him, “O Aba Abdillah عليه السلام, what are these hudud such that if one confesses to them before the Imam one single time against himself, the hadd is carried out upon him regarding them?” He said: “If he confesses against himself before the Imam to theft, he cuts off his hand; this is among the rights of Allah. If he confesses against himself that he drank wine, he administers the hadd to him; this is among the rights of Allah. And if he confesses against himself to zina while he is not muhsan, then this is among the rights of Allah.”

He said: “As for the rights of the Muslims, if he confesses against himself before the Imam to slander, he does not administer the hadd to him until the person slandered, or his guardian, is present. And if he confesses to killing a man, he does not kill him until the heirs of the slain person are present and demand the blood of their companion.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: As for what the beginning of this report contains, that a person’s confession against himself is accepted in every hadd among the hudud except zina, the basis for excluding zina from among the rest of the hudud is that in zina a confession must be made four times, and that is not so in any of the other hudud. There is nothing in it to indicate that his confession to zina is not accepted if he confesses four times. And that which indicates that a person’s confession against himself in zina is accepted, and that the hadd and stoning thereby become obligatory, is what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: “The thief is not cut off until he confesses to theft twice, and the fornicator is not stoned until he confesses four times.”

key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: stoning as a legal punishment in the stated case
key_terms.الزَّانِيَ الْمُحْصَنَ: a fornicator who is legally muhsan, for whom stoning is discussed
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the legitimate authority before whom legal confession is made and judicial rulings are carried out
key_terms.بِفِرْيَةٍ: a false accusation or slander for which hadd may apply
key_terms.حُدُودِ اللَّهِ: the divinely established penal limits and punishments
key_terms.حُقُوقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: rights belonging to other people, requiring their claim or presence

ai.seo_question: When is a confession before the Imam sufficient for establishing a hadd punishment in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning confession before the Imam in hadd cases, distinguishing between the rights of Allah and the rights of people. It explains when a single confession is sufficient, when the claimant or heirs must be present, and clarifies that zina requires repeated confession, with the compiler further reconciling the report through another narration.
